subject: FinTechCo - PII handling, residency & CMK options — post-demo follow-up
messages:
From: Aditya Rao <aditya@redwood.com>

Cc: Marissa Cole <marissa@redwood.com>

Subject: FinTechCo - PII handling, residency & CMK options — post-demo follow-up

Hi Elena / Sam,

Thanks again for taking the demo earlier today — good discussion. Per our call, I wanted to recap the key data handling and encryption points we covered and list concrete next steps so your security and infra teams can evaluate. I kept the items narrow so we can close this quickly.

Summary of requirements I captured:
- PII scope: credit card partials and user identifiers (email, phone) — keep within EU/US region boundaries per account.
- Data retention: customer prefers 90 days for PII payloads; request audit/log retention for 12 months.
- Logging/telemetry: request access controls on request/response logs and ability to mask PII fields.
- Residency: production inference in us-east-1 (primary) with eu-west-1 for DR; no cross-region replication of raw PII without opt-in.
- Encryption ask: TLS for in-transit; AES-256 at rest; customer-managed keys (BYOK) preferred with ability to rotate and revoke; HSM-backed CMKs for higher-assurance workloads.

What Redwood can provide (high level):
- In-transit: TLS 1.2+ (we can support TLS 1.3 on request).
- At-rest: data encrypted with AES-256; persistent storage encrypted using CMKs managed in customer or Redwood KMS depending on deployment (hosted vs private).
- BYOK: support for AWS KMS customer-managed keys (bring-your-own-key), including key rotation and aliasing. For customers needing HSM controls we integrate with CloudHSM / external HSMs in private deployments.
- Logs: request/response logs are encrypted at rest and access-controlled; PII redaction options (tokenization or masked copies) exist as a configuration.
- KV cache: ephemeral in-memory cache by default; persistent KV caching in dedicated environments encrypted by CMK.

Attachments included for your review: redwood-encryption-options-20260809.pdf (summary of BYOK/HSM paths and tradeoffs).

Proposed next steps:
1) Please confirm whether you want BYOK in your account (AWS KMS) vs Redwood-managed CMKs for the POC.
2) We’ll share SOC2 evidence and the short runbook for KMS integration (attached/linked).
3) Set up a 60-minute technical deep-dive with Rishi (our SE) to walk the team through KV cache behavior, key rotation, and test plan.

Available times this week: Aug 11 (10–12 PT) or Aug 12 (13–16 PT). Let me know what works.

Thanks —
Aditya Rao
Senior Account Executive | Redwood Inference
aditya@redwood.com | +1 (415) 555-0198

Subject: Re: FinTechCo - PII handling, residency & CMK options — post-demo follow-up

Aditya — thanks for the clear summary. A few clarifying items from security/infra: 

1) Tokenization / redaction: when you say PII redaction options, can you confirm whether Redwood supports live-tokenization (so tokens never leave our environment) vs server-side masking? We need to understand where raw values might be persisted in logs or caches.

2) KV cache and model context: is the cache ever written to disk in hosted deployments? If persistent caching is used we need encryption-at-rest with a CMK we control; also need the ability to rotate keys without breaking tokens.

3) CMK/HSM: Is the HSM path FIPS 140-2 Level 3 certified? We need that for higher-assurance customers. If not, what compensating controls do you provide?

4) Key separation: can we have a separate key per account/environment (not a single shared key)? Also want to understand exportability (can we export a wrapped key?) and the process for revoking access to a key if we terminate service.

If you can address those in a short note today that would help us prepare the runbook review. Also confirming our preference: BYOK (AWS KMS) for the POC unless there are blockers.

Best,
Elena Torres
Director, Security Engineering | FinTechCo
elena@fintechco.com
From: Aditya Rao <aditya@redwood.com>

Subject: Re: FinTechCo - PII handling, residency & CMK options — post-demo follow-up

Elena — great questions, answered inline below. I also attached our quick SOC2 evidence pack (fintech-qa-soc2-evidence.xlsx) and a short KMS integration runbook link for the devops team.

1) Tokenization / redaction
- Live-tokenization: supported in Redwood Private and in Dedicated deployments where the tokenization service can be run inside your VPC. For Hosted, we offer server-side masking or tokenization with a managed token service; tokens are stored encrypted (CMK) and can be configured to never appear in logs.
- Logs: by default, request/response logs capture metadata only; bodies with PII are redacted unless you opt in to full logging for debugging. We can also configure masking rules at field level.

2) KV cache and persistence
- Hosted (default): KV cache is in-memory and ephemeral (not written to disk).
- Dedicated/Private: persistent cache is supported and will be encrypted at rest using the CMK you provide (BYOK). Rotation is supported: we use AWS KMS envelope encryption so rotating a customer CMK updates the envelope keys without data corruption; we will walk through the rotation test during the SE call.

3) CMK/HSM (FIPS)
- Our hosted KMS integrations rely on AWS KMS which supports FIPS endpoints and CloudHSM where required. Redwood Private can be configured to use your CloudHSM or HSM appliance via our on-prem connector. If you require FIPS 140-2 Level 3, we will validate the HSM path and provide the cert matrix.

4) Key separation/export/revocation
- Separate keys per account/environment: supported via per-tenant CMK aliases in AWS KMS.
- Exportability: raw key material cannot be exported from a managed KMS (AWS KMS) — if you need exportable key material you will need an HSM that allows key export under your policy.
- Revocation/termination: if you revoke the CMK in your account, keys become unusable and data encrypted with that key becomes inaccessible. We document the termination steps in the runbook and can offer an orderly key rollover plan for exit.

Proposed immediate actions:
- I’ll schedule the SE deep-dive (Rishi) for Aug 12, 14:00 PT; please confirm or propose alternate.
- I’ll send the SOC2 artifact pack and the KMS runbook (links attached).

Link: https://drive.google.com/open?id=1a2B3cRunbook

Thanks —
Aditya

Elena / Team — quick technical notes ahead of the deep-dive:

- KV cache behavior: for hosted inference the cache is strictly in-memory per host and never persisted to disk. Eviction is LRU-based; encrypted in memory via process-local keys derived from the CMK (envelope encryption).

- Persistent caching in Dedicated/Private uses envelope encryption where the data key is generated per-node and encrypted by the customer CMK. This enables key rotation by re-encrypting the data key under the new CMK alias without re-writing every object.

- Logs and telemetry: we support field-level redaction before logs are persisted. Audit logs (who accessed what) are stored separately and encrypted with a different CMK and can be forwarded to your S3 with server-side encryption using your key.

- HSM compliance: we integrate with AWS CloudHSM (customer-owned cluster) and support HSM appliances for on-prem. For FIPS requirements we can provide the HSM certs and a mapping document showing which paths use hardware-backed keys vs software-wrapped keys. Action: I will attach the cert matrix and a short checklist during the SE call.

Action items from Rishi:
1) Share HSM/FIPS certificate matrix and KMS runbook (I’ll upload before the call).
2) Walkthrough of key rotation test plan during the deep-dive.
3) Provide a minimal reproducible test (sample request + key lifecycle steps) we can run in your staging account.

I’m available Aug 12 at 14:00 PT for the technical deep-dive. Please confirm.

Regards,
